title: Titanium Heat Shield for the Pylon Aft Fairing on VDK-56B Powered Aircraft

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: The aluminium heat shield in the pylon aft fairing is replaced by a titanium item with a revised standoff, after thermal distortion and fastener pull-through were reported on VDK-56B installations operating from hot-and-high airfields.

sections.reason: Distortion of the pylon aft fairing heat shield was reported on VDK-56B powered aircraft operating from hot-and-high airfields, with thirty-eight findings recorded over four years and eleven of them showing fastener pull-through at the standoff feet. The shield is not primary structure, but a detached panel in this position is a foreign object risk to the thrust reverser and it drives an unscheduled removal of the aft fairing to inspect. Skin temperature surveys taken on three aircraft showed peak values twenty-five degrees above the qualification temperature of the aluminium item during prolonged ground running.
sections.description: The aluminium heat shield is replaced by a titanium item of the same external profile, carried on the fitting D5450130082174 with lengthened standoffs that increase the ventilation gap by eight millimetres. The obsolete angle D5450007427818 at the forward attachment is deleted and the load is taken directly into the fairing frame with countersunk screws AES177340K7 in a closer pitch. The proximity indicator FIN 299PP and the fairing handle assembly FIN 70PP are unaffected but their brackets are re-drilled to clear the new standoff line. Work is done with the aft fairing removed, from zones 433, 443 and 481. Drawings D54501318343 issue C and D54500067210 issue E carry the shield layout and the standoff detail.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 2.1 kg per engine position, symmetric between engines, with no measurable balance effect. No electrical load change. The titanium shield is not interchangeable with the aluminium item because the standoff length and the screw pitch differ, and a mixed installation on one pylon is not permitted. The repeat inspection of the shield at every A check is replaced by a general visual at each C check. The modification is only released for VDK-56B installations; the equivalent condition does not arise on the VDK-12 pylon, which uses a different fairing.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z09673 in June 2018. Retrofit is a line-maintenance activity of about eight hours per pylon and is normally done at an A check with the aft fairing already open.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric between engine positions, no measurable effect
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z09673, no line stoppage
